name: Carmel Majidi
title: Clarence H. Adamson Professor of Mechanical Engineering
fitReason: The Soft Machines Lab has a concrete data-driven control line in addition to materials development. A supervised recurrent kinematics model supports reinforcement-learned soft-limb control, while September 2026 work extends modular learned proprioception.

physicalEvidence.summary: A May 2025 CMU master’s thesis, chaired by Majidi, deploys learned controllers on a real silicone/SMA limb through an Arduino and ROS2 loop. It tests spiral, square and letter trajectories, disturbances, changed limb stiffness and tip loads. The September 2026 continuum-robot paper demonstrates modular magnetic sensing with a learned joint-pose model on actual reconfigurable hardware. That newer paper’s autonomous closed-loop control is future work, so the 2025 thesis supplies the executed learned-control evidence.

unknowns: This is a soft hardware and sensing lab with a substantial demonstrated learning/control thread, not a dedicated foundation-model manipulation group.

The 2025 learned controller is trained in a learned-kinematics environment before physical deployment. Waypoint progression uses a ten-degree bending-angle tolerance; it is not millimeter-precision manipulation. The DQN safety-filter test needs a conservative tuned threshold because of sim-to-real error and does not establish unconditional hardware safety.
The September 2026 paper predicts joint pose from onboard magnetic measurements. Grasp/traversal demonstrations do not establish an autonomously learned end-to-end manipulation policy.

The current official named professorship is in Mechanical Engineering. Robotics Institute lists a courtesy appointment and corroborates lab affiliation/advised students. The existing CMU central visitor policy does not itself establish this lab’s capacity or summer 2027 authorization.
